paragraphs.text: I say then, Did God cast off his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
paragraphs.original: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ Ἰσραηλίτης εἰμί, ἐκ σπέρματος Ἀβραάμ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν.
paragraphs.translit: Legō oun, mē apōsato ho theos ton laon autou; mē genoito· kai gar egō Israēlitēs eimi, ek spermatos Abraam, phylēs Beniamin.

paragraphs.text: God did not cast off his people which he foreknew. Or know ye not what the scripture saith of Elijah? how he pleadeth with God against Israel:
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν προέγνω. ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ;
paragraphs.translit: ouk apōsato ho theos ton laon autou hon proegnō. ē ouk oidate en Ēlia ti legei hē graphē, hōs entynchanei tō theō kata tou Israēl;

paragraphs.text: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, they have digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.
paragraphs.original: Κύριε, τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν, τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν, κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος, καὶ ζητοῦσιν τὴν ψυχήν μου.
paragraphs.translit: Kyrie, tous prophētas sou apekteinan, ta thysiastēria sou kateskapsan, kagō hypeleiphthēn monos, kai zētousin tēn psychēn mou.

paragraphs.text: But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have left for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to Baal.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ χρηματισμός; Κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτακισχιλίους ἄνδρας, οἵτινες οὐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ.
paragraphs.translit: alla ti legei autō ho chrēmatismos; Katelipon emautō heptakischilious andras, hoitines ouk ekampsan gony tē Baal.

paragraphs.text: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως οὖν καὶ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατʼ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν·
paragraphs.translit: houtōs oun kai en tō nyn kairō leimma katʼ eklogēn charitos gegonen·

paragraphs.text: But if it is by grace, it is no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ χάριτι, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκέτι γίνεται χάρις.
paragraphs.translit: ei de chariti, ouketi ex ergōn, epei hē charis ouketi ginetai charis.

paragraphs.text: What then? that which Israel seeketh for, that he obtained not; but the election obtained it, and the rest were hardened:
paragraphs.original: τί οὖν; ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραήλ, τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν, ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν· οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν,
paragraphs.translit: ti oun; ho epizētei Israēl, touto ouk epetychen, hē de eklogē epetychen· hoi de loipoi epōrōthēsan,

paragraphs.text: according as it is written, God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, unto this very day.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως, ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gegraptai· Edōken autois ho theos pneuma katanyxeōs, ophthalmous tou mē blepein kai ōta tou mē akouein, heōs tēs sēmeron hēmeras.

paragraphs.text: And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, And a stumblingblock, and a recompense unto them:
paragraphs.original: καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει· Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς θήραν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδομα αὐτοῖς,
paragraphs.translit: kai Dauid legei· Genēthētō hē trapeza autōn eis pagida kai eis thēran kai eis skandalon kai eis antapodoma autois,

paragraphs.text: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, And bow thou down their back always.
paragraphs.original: σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον.
paragraphs.translit: skotisthētōsan hoi ophthalmoi autōn tou mē blepein, kai ton nōton autōn dia pantos synkampson.

paragraphs.text: I say then, Did they stumble that they might fall? God forbid: but by their fall salvation [is come] unto the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.
paragraphs.original: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσιν; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Legō oun, mē eptaisan hina pesōsin; mē genoito· alla tō autōn paraptōmati hē sōtēria tois ethnesin, eis to parazēlōsai autous.

paragraphs.text: Now if their fall, is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ei de to paraptōma autōn ploutos kosmou kai to hēttēma autōn ploutos ethnōn, posō mallon to plērōma autōn.

paragraphs.text: But I speak to you that are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;
paragraphs.original: Ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. ἐφʼ ὅσον μὲν οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος, τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω,
paragraphs.translit: Hymin de legō tois ethnesin. ephʼ hoson men oun eimi egō ethnōn apostolos, tēn diakonian mou doxazō,

paragraphs.text: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy [them that are] my flesh, and may save some of them.
paragraphs.original: εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ei pōs parazēlōsō mou tēn sarka kai sōsō tinas ex autōn.

paragraphs.text: For if the casting away of them [is] the reconciling of the world, what [shall] the receiving [of them be], but life from the dead?
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου, τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν;
paragraphs.translit: ei gar hē apobolē autōn katallagē kosmou, tis hē proslēmpsis ei mē zōē ek nekrōn;

paragraphs.text: And if the firstfruit is holy, so is the lump: and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀπαρχὴ ἁγία, καὶ τὸ φύραμα· καὶ εἰ ἡ ῥίζα ἁγία, καὶ οἱ κλάδοι.
paragraphs.translit: ei de hē aparchē hagia, kai to phyrama· kai ei hē rhiza hagia, kai hoi kladoi.

paragraphs.text: But if some of the branches were broken off, and thou, being a wild olive, wast grafted in among them, and didst become partaker with them of the root of the fatness of the olive tree;
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δέ τινες τῶν κλάδων ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ ἀγριέλαιος ὢν ἐνεκεντρίσθης ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ συγκοινωνὸς τῆς ῥίζης τῆς πιότητος τῆς ἐλαίας ἐγένου,
paragraphs.translit: Ei de tines tōn kladōn exeklasthēsan, sy de agrielaios ōn enekentristhēs en autois kai synkoinōnos tēs rhizēs tēs piotētos tēs elaias egenou,

paragraphs.text: glory not over the branches: but if thou gloriest, it is not thou that bearest the root, but the root thee.
paragraphs.original: μὴ κατακαυχῶ τῶν κλάδων· εἰ δὲ κατακαυχᾶσαι, οὐ σὺ τὴν ῥίζαν βαστάζεις ἀλλὰ ἡ ῥίζα σέ.
paragraphs.translit: mē katakauchō tōn kladōn· ei de katakauchasai, ou sy tēn rhizan bastazeis alla hē rhiza se.

paragraphs.text: Thou wilt say then, Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.
paragraphs.original: ἐρεῖς οὖν· Ἐξεκλάσθησαν κλάδοι ἵνα ἐγὼ ἐγκεντρισθῶ.
paragraphs.translit: ereis oun· Exeklasthēsan kladoi hina egō enkentristhō.

paragraphs.text: Well; by their unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by thy faith. Be not highminded, but fear:
paragraphs.original: καλῶς· τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ τῇ πίστει ἕστηκας. μὴ ὑψηλὰ φρόνει, ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kalōs· tē apistia exeklasthēsan, sy de tē pistei hestēkas. mē hypsēla phronei, alla phobou·

paragraphs.text: for if God spared not the natural branches, neither will he spare thee.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τῶν κατὰ φύσιν κλάδων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, οὐδὲ σοῦ φείσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar ho theos tōn kata physin kladōn ouk epheisato, oude sou pheisetai.

paragraphs.text: Behold then the goodness and severity of God: toward them that fell, severity; but toward thee, God`s goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.
paragraphs.original: ἴδε οὖν χρηστότητα καὶ ἀποτομίαν θεοῦ· ἐπὶ μὲν τοὺς πεσόντας ἀποτομία, ἐπὶ δὲ σὲ χρηστότης θεοῦ, ἐὰν ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι, ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ἐκκοπήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: ide oun chrēstotēta kai apotomian theou· epi men tous pesontas apotomia, epi de se chrēstotēs theou, ean epimenēs tē chrēstotēti, epei kai sy ekkopēsē.

paragraphs.text: And they also, if they continue not in their unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖνοι δέ, ἐὰν μὴ ἐπιμένωσι τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, ἐγκεντρισθήσονται· δυνατὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς πάλιν ἐγκεντρίσαι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kakeinoi de, ean mē epimenōsi tē apistia, enkentristhēsontai· dynatos gar estin ho theos palin enkentrisai autous.

paragraphs.text: For if thou wast cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and wast grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree; how much more shall these, which are the natural [branches], be grafted into their own olive tree?
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐκ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν ἐξεκόπης ἀγριελαίου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν ἐνεκεντρίσθης εἰς καλλιέλαιον, πόσῳ μᾶλλον οὗτοι οἱ κατὰ φύσιν ἐγκεντρισθήσονται τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐλαίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar sy ek tēs kata physin exekopēs agrielaiou kai para physin enekentristhēs eis kallielaion, posō mallon houtoi hoi kata physin enkentristhēsontai tē idia elaia.

paragraphs.text: For I would not, brethren, have you ignorant of this mystery, lest ye be wise in your own conceits, that a hardening in part hath befallen Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in;
paragraphs.original: Οὐ γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο, ἵνα μὴ ἦτε ἑαυτοῖς φρόνιμοι, ὅτι πώρωσις ἀπὸ μέρους τῷ Ἰσραὴλ γέγονεν ἄχρι οὗ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ,
paragraphs.translit: Ou gar thelō hymas agnoein, adelphoi, to mystērion touto, hina mē ēte heautois phronimoi, hoti pōrōsis apo merous tō Israēl gegonen achri hou to plērōma tōn ethnōn eiselthē,

paragraphs.text: and so all Israel shall be saved: even as it is written, There shall come out of Zion the Deliverer; He shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὕτως πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται· καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἥξει ἐκ Σιὼν ὁ ῥυόμενος, ἀποστρέψει ἀσεβείας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβ.
paragraphs.translit: kai houtōs pas Israēl sōthēsetai· kathōs gegraptai· Hēxei ek Siōn ho rhyomenos, apostrepsei asebeias apo Iakōb.

paragraphs.text: And this is my covenant unto them, When I shall take away their sins.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἡ παρʼ ἐμοῦ διαθήκη, ὅταν ἀφέλωμαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hautē autois hē parʼ emou diathēkē, hotan aphelōmai tas hamartias autōn.

paragraphs.text: As touching the gospel, they are enemies for your sake: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers` sake.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ μὲν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἐχθροὶ διʼ ὑμᾶς, κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἐκλογὴν ἀγαπητοὶ διὰ τοὺς πατέρας·
paragraphs.translit: kata men to euangelion echthroi diʼ hymas, kata de tēn eklogēn agapētoi dia tous pateras·

paragraphs.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are not repented of.
paragraphs.original: ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα καὶ ἡ κλῆσις τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ametamelēta gar ta charismata kai hē klēsis tou theou.

paragraphs.text: For as ye in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε τῷ θεῷ, νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ,
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar hymeis pote ēpeithēsate tō theō, nyn de ēleēthēte tē toutōn apeitheia,

paragraphs.text: even so have these also now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they also may now obtain mercy.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ οὗτοι νῦν ἠπείθησαν τῷ ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ νῦν ἐλεηθῶσιν·
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai houtoi nyn ēpeithēsan tō hymeterō eleei hina kai autoi nyn eleēthōsin·

paragraphs.text: For God hath shut up all unto disobedience, that he might have mercy upon all.
paragraphs.original: συνέκλεισεν γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τοὺς πάντας εἰς ἀπείθειαν ἵνα τοὺς πάντας ἐλεήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: synekleisen gar ho theos tous pantas eis apeitheian hina tous pantas eleēsē.

paragraphs.text: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!
paragraphs.original: Ὦ βάθος πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως θεοῦ· ὡς ἀνεξεραύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ō bathos ploutou kai sophias kai gnōseōs theou· hōs anexeraunēta ta krimata autou kai anexichniastoi hai hodoi autou.

paragraphs.text: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor?
paragraphs.original: Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;
paragraphs.translit: Tis gar egnō noun kyriou; ē tis symboulos autou egeneto;

paragraphs.text: or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again?
paragraphs.original: ἢ τίς προέδωκεν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνταποδοθήσεται αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: ē tis proedōken autō, kai antapodothēsetai autō;

paragraphs.text: For of him, and through him, and unto him, are all things. To him [be] the glory for ever. Amen.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ διʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ἀμήν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ex autou kai diʼ autou kai eis auton ta panta· autō hē doxa eis tous aiōnas, amēn.
